untrustedWorkspaces.description: VMDE renders and edits markdown, but defers writing images and creating wiki pages until the workspace is trusted.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Editing works; features that depend on the local filesystem (image upload, wiki page creation, asset resolution) are unavailable in virtual workspaces.

enumDescriptions: Reopen in whatever mode you last used (the previous behaviour).
Instant Rendering — markdown syntax reveals itself around the cursor.
WYSIWYG — markers stay hidden while you type.
Split — source on the left, live preview on the right.
Preview — open read-only; switch to editing from the toolbar.
vmde.editor.defaultMode.description: Default mode for opening Markdown files. You can override it per path with Default Mode by Glob. Large files always use Instant Rendering.

vmde.editor.defaultModeByGlob.markdownDescription: Per-path overrides for `#vmde.editor.defaultMode#`, keyed by glob against the workspace-relative path — for example `{ "docs/**": "preview" }`. A matching glob wins over the flat setting. Supports `**`, `*` and `?`.

vmde.editor.fullWidth.description: Use the full editor width, with the same side margins as VS Code's built-in markdown preview. Turn off for a narrow view: the text column is capped at 800px and centered.

vmde.editor.fontSize.description: Editor content size. Use "editor" to follow VS Code, "vditor" for 16px, or enter a pixel value such as "15".

vmde.editor.toolbar.description: Show the editor toolbar. When off, the editor opens without a toolbar.

vmde.editor.headingMarkers.description: Show heading and link-reference markers in Instant Rendering mode. Disable to reduce the left margin.

vmde.editor.headingColors.description: Apply a themed background to headings (h1–h6) for easier scanning.

vmde.editor.codeLineNumbers.description: Show line numbers in fenced code blocks (rendered preview). Off by default — adds a line-number gutter per code block.

vmde.editor.modifierClickLinks.description: Open links with Ctrl+click (Cmd+click on macOS). Disable to open links with a regular click instead.

enumDescriptions: GitHub's heading-anchor algorithm (github-slugger).
GitLab's heading-anchor algorithm — differs from GitHub only for rare Unicode connector-punctuation characters.
vmde.editor.slugifyMode.description: Heading-anchor format used for #heading links, the outline, and link completion.

vmde.restorePosition.description: Reopen Markdown documents at the last viewed block and caret position. Explicit navigation and input during loading take priority.

enumDescriptions: Convert TAB-separated blocks only — what Excel, Sheets and Numbers put on the clipboard.
Also convert comma-separated blocks. Off by default: two lines of comma-ful prose genuinely look like CSV.
Never convert; paste the text as-is.
vmde.paste.csvFormat.description: Convert pasted spreadsheet cells to a Markdown table. Content pasted into code blocks stays unchanged.

vmde.paste.urlAsLink.description: Convert pasted URLs to Markdown links. With selected text, the selection becomes the link label.

enumDescriptions: Match the VS Code theme's colors, following the active light/dark theme.
Render the markdown like GitHub's light theme, regardless of the VS Code theme.
Render the markdown like GitHub's dark theme, regardless of the VS Code theme.
Material Dark (One Dark) palette, regardless of the VS Code theme.
VS Code's built-in markdown preview — Light 2026 (the VS Code 1.123+ light default), regardless of the VS Code theme.
VS Code's built-in markdown preview — Dark 2026 (the VS Code 1.123+ dark default), regardless of the VS Code theme.
vmde.theme.content.description: Rendered Markdown color theme. "auto" follows VS Code; named themes use their own palette. Configure code colors separately.

enumDescriptions: Follow the VS Code light/dark theme — github in a light theme, github-dark in a dark one.
vmde.theme.code.description: Syntax-highlight theme for code blocks. "auto" follows the VS Code theme; otherwise choose a specific theme.

vmde.editor.wrapColumn.markdownDescription: Column used by manual Rewrap and #vmde.editor.autoWrap#. Words longer than the column are left intact.

vmde.editor.autoWrap.markdownDescription: Automatically wrap eligible source Markdown at #vmde.editor.wrapColumn# after #vmde.editor.autoWrapDelay#. IR and WYSIWYG always render soft line breaks as spaces.

vmde.editor.autoWrapDelay.markdownDescription: Idle delay in milliseconds before automatic wrapping. Ignored unless #vmde.editor.autoWrap# is enabled.

vmde.preview.reflowLineBreaks.markdownDescription: Reflow soft line breaks on Preview surfaces like GitHub and VS Code. This is independent from #vmde.editor.autoWrap#, which only formats source Markdown.

vmde.markdown.toc.markdownDescription: Render #[toc]# as a navigable table of contents. Off by default because it changes existing document parsing.

vmde.markdown.mark.markdownDescription: Render #==text==# as highlighted text. Off by default because it changes existing document parsing.

vmde.markdown.supSub.markdownDescription: Enable Lute superscript and subscript syntax. When enabled, #~text~# is subscript instead of strikethrough; #~~text~~# remains strikethrough.

enumDescriptions: Dagre — Mermaid's default layered layout (appearance unchanged).
ELK — Eclipse Layout Kernel: tighter graphs with orthogonal edge routing. Applies to graph diagrams (flowchart, class, state, ER).
vmde.diagram.mermaid.layout.description: Layout engine for Mermaid graph diagrams. Use ELK for more compact graphs; other Mermaid diagram types are unaffected.

enumDescriptions: Follow the VS Code editor theme — uses the content theme's paired palette if any (e.g. github-light/dark), else mermaid's own dark/default (a plain flowchart looks mostly monochrome).
Mermaid's default colour palette.
Force the dark palette regardless of the editor theme.
The "forest" colour palette (greens).
The "neutral" colour palette (greyscale-ish, print-friendly).
VS Code — light (matches the vscode-light-2026 content theme).
VS Code — dark (matches the vscode-dark-2026 content theme).
Zinc — light (neutral greys).
Zinc — dark (neutral greys).
Tokyo Night (dark, blue/purple).
Tokyo Night Storm (dark, slightly lighter).
Tokyo Night — light.
Catppuccin Mocha (dark, pastel).
Catppuccin Latte (light, pastel).
Nord (dark, arctic blue).
Nord — light.
Dracula (dark, purple/pink).
GitHub — light (matches the github-light content theme).
GitHub — dark (matches the github-dark content theme).
Solarized — light.
Solarized — dark.
One Dark (Atom).
vmde.diagram.mermaid.theme.description: Color theme for Mermaid diagrams. "auto" follows the VS Code theme; otherwise choose a specific theme.

enumDescriptions: Dagre — hierarchical layout with straight/curved edges.
ELK (original) — Eclipse Layout Kernel orthogonal layout.
Optimised Layout engine for D2 diagrams
vmde.diagram.d2.layout.description: Layout engine for D2 diagrams — how the diagrams are drawn.

enumDescriptions: Auto — pair the palette to the active content theme + editor light/dark, transparent page (blends into the editor, like mermaid/echarts).
D2 Neutral default — blue borders/edges, lavender fills, white page (the canonical d2 look).
D2 Neutral grey — greyscale borders + fills, white page.
D2 Cool classics — vivid blue palette, white page.
D2 Terminal — black borders, light fills, white page.
D2 Dark mauve — dark page (#1E1E2E) with mauve accents (the dark d2 theme).
VS Code Light — subtle accent-tinted fills, transparent page (blends into a light editor, mermaid-style).
VS Code Dark — cyan accents, transparent page (blends into a dark editor, mermaid-style).
GitHub Light — subtle blue-tinted fills, transparent page (blends into a light editor, mermaid-style).
GitHub Dark — blue accents, transparent page (blends into a dark editor, mermaid-style).
Monochrome — transparent background, lines follow the editor foreground (currentColor).
vmde.diagram.d2.theme.description: Color theme for D2 diagrams. "auto" follows the render theme; "mono" uses the editor foreground.

vmde.diagram.d2.sketch.description: Use a hand-drawn style for D2 diagrams. Colors still follow the selected D2 theme.

enumDescriptions: Follow the rendering theme (vmde.theme.content) — pairs each content theme with a matching palette (e.g. github-light/dark); when the content theme is "auto", follows the VS Code editor's own colors.
A neutral light theme (white background).
A neutral dark theme (dark background).
Vintage — muted, warm retro palette (light background).
Macarons — soft pastel palette.
Infographic — bright, high-contrast palette.
Roma — earthy red/brown palette.
Shine — vivid saturated palette.
Tech Blue — cool blue palette.
Vintage Dark — the vintage palette on a warm dark background.
vmde.diagram.echarts.theme.description: Color theme for ECharts charts. "auto" follows the rendering theme (and the VS Code editor when that is "auto"); otherwise choose a neutral light/dark or one of ECharts' built-in gallery themes.

enumDescriptions: Monochrome CARTO basemap (Positron / Dark Matter) that follows the editor's light/dark theme — a neutral backdrop for your data (the default).
CARTO Voyager — a colored street basemap.
OpenStreetMap standard — a full-color basemap.
No basemap — draw only the GeoJSON/TopoJSON geometry on a transparent canvas.
vmde.diagram.geo.basemap.description: Basemap for GeoJSON and TopoJSON maps. Remote tiles require Allow Remote Images; "none" works offline.

vmde.css.external.description: External CSS files to load in the editor. Paths may be absolute or workspace-relative; changes reload automatically.

vmde.outline.defaultOpen.description: Open the outline panel automatically when an editor opens.

vmde.outline.tree.description: Show the 'Markdown Outline' tree in the Explorer sidebar (a clickable heading list for the open markdown file). Turn off to hide it.

vmde.outline.position.description: Which side the outline panel opens on.

vmde.outline.highlight.description: Briefly flash a heading when you click it in the outline.

vmde.image.saveFolder.description: Destination folder for uploaded files. The default `assets` follows a matching `markdown.copyFiles.destination` rule; set another value here to override it. Use `${projectRoot}/assets` for a project-level folder.

enumDescriptions: Keep uploaded/pasted images in their original format and bytes.
Convert raster uploads to WebP (smaller files). SVG and animated GIF are always kept as-is.
vmde.image.format.description: Output format for uploaded and pasted images. WebP reduces raster image size; SVG and GIF files keep their original format.

vmde.image.quality.markdownDescription: WebP quality (1–100) when `#vmde.image.format#` is `webp`. Higher is larger and sharper; 80 is a good size/quality balance. Ignored for `original`.

vmde.image.maxWidth.markdownDescription: Resize uploaded and pasted images wider than this value. Use 0 to disable resizing.

vmde.image.allowRemote.markdownDescription: Allow remote HTTPS images in the editor. Disabled by default because loading them can reveal your IP and that you opened the file. Reopen the editor after changing this setting.

vmde.wiki.enabled.description: Enable wiki-link rendering ([[Page Name]] chips, navigation, and page creation).

vmde.wiki.root.description: Wiki root folder (relative to the workspace root). Leave empty to use the workspace root. Example: `docs/wiki`.

vmde.performance.streamLargeFiles.description: Load large Markdown files in chunks to keep the editor responsive. Files around 700 KB or larger use this automatically.

vmde.performance.contentVisibility.description: Improve large-document performance by skipping off-screen layout and painting. Reopen the file after changing this setting.
